description: Hi! We are Team AstroPhysio!We are a team of passionate Physiotherapy students from Cairo, Egypt, who love space, human health, and technology.Our skills: Muscle assessment, physiotherapy, human anatomy, health monitoring, and creative problem-solving.Our project for this hackathon is FLEXAURA - a smart wearable to monitor astronaut muscles and vitals in space.hardworking. ail!We are looking for:A developer / UI designer / video editor who can help us build the app prototype and presentation.
summary: FLEXAURA is a dual-mode wearable health system built by Team AstroPhysio. In Wrist Mode, it continuously monitors heart rate and VO2 fitness. In Scan Mode, the detachable pod is placed on any muscle (Soleus, Quadriceps, Biceps) to measure strength via EMG vs. pre-flight baseline. Data is logged daily and synced weekly. Our core intelligence is based on NASA-STD-3001: alerts trigger if muscle <80% [V1 4024], bone risk [V1 4027/4028], or vitals drop, enabling predictive countermeasures DAYS before failure.
details: FlexAura is a wearable health-monitoring system for astronauts on long-duration missions. It combines a smart bracelet system with a companion web application, AstroPhysio. The AstroPhysio app is built and working as a prototype; the bracelet is the concept the app is designed to receive data from. THE PROBLEM 1. Muscles and bones weaken in microgravity. The antigravity (postural) muscles, such as the calves, quadriceps and spinal extensors, lose strength and range of motion fastest, because gravity no longer loads them. 2. Earth is far, and the link is not always there. Precise, continuous follow-up that reaches Earth on a regular basis is limited, so medical support can be delayed or interrupted, and decline is often discovered only after the astronaut returns to Earth. This applies to every vital sign: heart rate, blood oxygen, blood pressure and stress. 3. Numbers alone are easy to miss. A value only helps if it is compared to a clear limit and followed by a clear action. THE SOLUTION The FlexAura bracelet works in two modes: - Wrist mode: worn like a regular bracelet, it continuously measures heart rate, blood pressure, blood oxygen (SpO2) and other vital signs, and monitors stress level. - Muscle mode: placed directly on a specific muscle, it measures exactly the values we need for that muscle, such as range of motion and strength, using sensors such as an electrogoniometer. Automatic alerts: as soon as any value leaves its normal range, the system sends the alert to Earth automatically and, at the same moment, notifies the astronaut so they can act right away (for example, by doing resistance exercises). Automatic daily reports: every day at the same fixed time (for example 12 AM), a report with all the tracked measurements of that day is sent to Earth automatically. The ground team receives a complete daily picture and can detect muscle atrophy or any other decline while it is happening, instead of after the mission ends. HOW THE APP WORKS (PROTOTYPE) 1. Save a personal baseline once. 2. Enter daily raw measurements. 3. The app converts them to a percentage of the baseline. 4. It compares them with NASA limits. 5. It raises a red alert and an alarm sound, suggests resistance exercises with training videos, and prepares daily and weekly reports. Alerts are queued for Earth at the moment they appear, and the daily report is queued automatically at 12 AM. The app runs fully offline in the browser. A Service Worker caches it, and the data stays on the device, stored in IndexedDB and encrypted with AES-GCM. Reports and alerts wait in an "Earth link" outbox until a link is available. NASA DATA USED We used NASA-STD-3001 Volume 1 Rev C (Crew Health) as the source of every alert limit: - [V1 4024] Muscle strength: at least 80% of baseline. Red alert and alarm below 80%. - [V1 4027] Bone density, hip and spine: at least 95%. Red alert and alarm below 95%. - [V1 4027] Bone density, femoral neck: at least 90%. Red alert and alarm below 90%. These are the only alert limits in the app. Heart rate, sleep, steps, blood oxygen, blood pressure and range of motion are recorded and reported, but have no alarm because we did not find a NASA limit for them. We did not use NASA datasets. All demo values are simulated and are not real astronaut data. TOOLS AND LANGUAGES HTML, CSS and JavaScript, Canvas charts, Web Audio API (alarm sound), IndexedDB, Web Crypto API, Service Worker, and GitHub Pages for hosting. CURRENT LIMITS AND NEXT STEPS The bracelet hardware and stress monitoring are concepts and have not been built. In the prototype, data come from simulated data, manual entry or CSV import, and sending to Earth is simulated (no real server). This is a decision-support prototype, not a medical device. Next steps: read measurements from real sensors, send reports to Earth over a real link, and a clinical review of the exercises by a physical therapist.
